article.title: Turkey Bans Media Reporting on Deadly Factory Blast in Izmir
article.description: Authorities ban media from reporting deadly factory blast in Izmir province that has killed 17 workers, prompting concerns over public's right to access information.
paragraphs: Turkey’s broadcasting regulator, the Radio and Television Supreme Council, RTUK, on Monday announced a ban on reporting an explosion at an iron and steel factory in Aliaga, Izmir that has cost 17 lives.
“A ban has been imposed on all news reports, interviews and commentary concerning the incident in print, visual and social media, as well as online, until the investigation is completed,” RTUK said.

Authorities said the ban was intended to prevent disinformation and public unrest, protect public order and ensure the investigation could proceed properly. Turkey has previously introduced reporting bans when there have been terror attacks, natural disasters, fatal accidents and major police operations targeting critics.
In 2025, for example, the RTUK issued a broadcasting ban about a fire in a ski resort that killed 66 holidaymakers. Critics say that the practice undermines the public’s right to access information.
The death toll from Monday’s blast rose to 17, while 14 workers were injured.

(DHA Photo) by Daily Sabah with AA Nov 10, 2026 2:58 pm Authorities in Türkiye have ordered the detention of 11 suspects in connection with an explosion at a steel plant in Izmir , western Türkiye, that killed 17 workers on Monday, Deputy Justice Minister Can Tuncay said Tuesday.

The suspects include the factory manager, the steelworks manager, maintenance and engineering personnel, the company’s Aliağa branch manager and its board chairperson, Tuncay told reporters after inspecting the site in Aliağa district.

The explosion occurred Monday at the HABAŞ iron and steel plant during steelmaking operations. According to Tuncay, the blast happened when a crane runway beam detached from its columns, supports and connections while a vessel associated with the plant’s third electric arc furnace was being moved. The beam, charging crane and vessel fell, triggering the explosion.

Some 17 workers were killed, while one of the injured remained in critical condition, Tuncay said. One worker was still unaccounted for following an application by the family, and inspections at the site continued.

A preliminary expert report had been received, Tuncay said, adding that further assessments would be conducted as the investigation progressed. He said the Aliağa Chief Public Prosecutor’s Office was continuing its examination with the assistance of gendarmerie teams until the on-site procedures were completed.

article.title: At least nine detained protesting at blast-hit Turkiye steel plant
article.description: Nine people were detained by Turkish security forces for protesting a ban on mobile phones at a steel plant following a deadly explosion. The workers gathered at the plant’s entrance to express their discontent.
paragraphs: Aliaga, Turkiye: Turkiye’s security forces on Friday detained at least nine people protesting a ban on bringing mobile phones into a steel plant that was hit by a deadly explosion this week, a workers’ collective said.

Workers arriving for their morning shift at the HABAS steel factory were told to leave their mobile phones at a security checkpoint, prompting them to gather at the facility’s entrance in protest, according to Oktay Turk, spokesman for the Aegean Workers’ Collective.

“At least nine people were detained,” Turk told AFP, adding that he was among those taken into custody at the factory, located in Aliaga, a district known for shipbreaking and heavy industry near the western port city of Izmir.
The mobile phone ban was introduced by HABAS chairman Mehmet Rustu Basaran, who was placed under house arrest as part of an investigation into Monday’s explosion, Turk said.
A company notice said mobile phones would no longer be allowed inside.

article.title: IFJ Scrubs 40 Gaza Journalist Names Amid Hamas Ties
article.description: IFJ quietly dropped roughly 40 names from its Gaza journalist list, including dozens linked by watchdogs to Hamas and Islamic Jihad.
paragraphs: IFJ quietly dropped roughly 40 names from its Gaza journalist list, including dozens linked by watchdogs to Hamas and Islamic Jihad.

Print Facebook Twitter Telegram LinkedIn WhatsApp Email Pinterest Digg Buffer Pocket Blogger Yahoo Mail Flipboard Viber Facebook Messenger Copy Link The International Federation of Journalists (IFJ) has quite an accuracy problem with its Gaza casualty list. Roughly 40 names have awkwardly and quietly been taken off since October without any editorial note, many of the names belonging to men identified as Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad fighters. The IFJ has not publicly explained the removals.

It took two watchdog groups, CAMERA and HonestReporting, reviewing older versions of the website to uncover these stealth edits. On October 3rd, the list was around 240 journalists and media workers who were named as killed in Gaza. That fell to 203 by October 8th, then dropped another three stealthily by the time the Free Beacon released its report.
However, the anti-Israeli IFJ continues to make sweeping generalizations and accusations against Israel on that same website:
“…the Israeli army has deliberately targeted journalists, and some of these cases are currently the subject of a complaint file before the International Criminal Court.”

paragraphs: HOME NEWS Region City India World BUSINESS EDITORIAL OPINION SPORTS GALLERY EPAPER Kashmir Reader HOME NEWS Region City India World BUSINESS EDITORIAL OPINION SPORTS GALLERY EPAPER World ‘Israeli strike kills three in vehicle distributing aid in Gaza’ By Agencies 9:46 am November 22, 2026 0 0 Share Facebook X Pinterest WhatsApp Must read Bhagat calls for effective implementation of EODB reforms, legal metrology laws 8:54 am November 21, 2026 Elderly care a social & moral responsibility: Rajnath Singh 1:07 am November 18, 2026 Rifle Threat Case: Court denies bail to retired DySP’s son 1:27 am November 18, 2026 Police reunite missing child with family 1:07 am November 18, 2026 Agencies https://kashmirreader.com JERUSALEM: An Israeli strike killed three Palestinians in a vehicle carrying papers and food for the World Central Kitchen charity in Gaza City on Saturday, according to Gaza’s health ministry and eyewitnesses. The Israeli military said several militant operatives were targeted in the area without providing further details. It did not immediately respond to questions on why it had hit a vehicle that appeared to be distributing aid. World Central Kitchen did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The vehicle appeared to be carrying packaged foodstuffs, and papers ⁠inside carried the ⁠logo of World Central Kitchen, an aid organization that distributes food in Gaza, according to a Reuters witness. “It was just about to stop to distribute the food and drink to children when it was hit by a missile,” said Abu Zein Al-Daya, who also witnessed the strike. Afterwards, meals of cooked rice were scattered around the vehicle, which was partially covered in the ⁠blood of the victims of the attack. ISRAELI STRIKES CONTINUE IN GAZA The Israeli military previously killed seven World Central Kitchen workers in a 2024 strike, including citizens of Australia, Britain and Poland. At the time, the military said there had been “serious errors and breaches of procedure” but in 2026 it said it had found no basis upon which to open criminal investigations into the incident. Israel briefly launched a ground operation in Gaza earlier this week and killed six in a strike on a hospital that it said was targeting a Hamas commander. An October 2025 US-backed ceasefire halted major fighting in the shattered ⁠territory but ⁠has not stopped Israeli attacks on Gaza or secured Hamas’ disarmament. At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed in the time since, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies. Israeli troops now control around two-thirds of Gaza, up from more than half at the time of the ceasefire, with Hamas controlling a sliver of territory along Gaza’s coast. Israel’s more than two-year-long assault on Gaza has killed tens of thousands, caused a hunger crisis, internally displaced Gaza’s entire population and led to assessments of genocide from scholars and a United Nations inquiry. Israel calls its actions self-defense after Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took more than 250 hostages in an October 2023 attack. Reuters

article.title: Six Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza, civil defence says
paragraphs: Israeli strikes killed six people in the Gaza Strip on Friday, the civil defence agency in the war-shattered territory told AFP, despite a ceasefire.

Mahmoud Bassal, the spokesman for Gaza's civil defence agency, said that four Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in an Israeli airstrike southwest of Bureij refugee camp in the central Gaza Strip on Friday.
The civil defence also said one Palestinian was killed in an Israeli drone strike targeting a tent in the Al-Munasara camp for displaced people in Deir al-Balah.
Another person was killed in a drone strike north of Nuseirat refugee camp, also in the central Gaza Strip.
The Israeli military told AFP it had "targeted multiple military operatives" in several strikes, which came a day after the army said it had completed a ground incursion in the central Gaza Strip.

article.title: Saudi Arabia Replaces War Commander as Houthis Close In on Aden - Voice of Vienna
article.description: Saudi Arabia has replaced the commander of its coalition forces in Yemen, a sign of how heavily the war is weighing on Riyadh as Houthi fighters creep toward the government’s temporary capital, Aden. paragraphs: Saudi Arabia has replaced the commander of its coalition forces in Yemen, a sign of how heavily the war is weighing on Riyadh as Houthi fighters creep toward the government’s temporary capital, Aden.

In a decree issued Monday and carried by Saudi state media, King Salman named General Fayyad al-Ruwaili to lead the coalition. He replaces Lieutenant General Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman, who was made a military adviser to the defense minister, one day after coalition forces were forced to pull back, according to Al Jazeera News.

That withdrawal was a heavy blow. On Sunday, Yemen’s internationally recognized government said its forces were leaving positions near the Bab al-Mandeb strait to concentrate on defending Aden. The strait matters far beyond Yemen: Saudi oil exports now flow through it while the US-Iran war chokes traffic in the Strait of Hormuz. The Houthis, meanwhile, have fired ballistic missiles at Saudi airports and oil facilities since the civil war reignited in July.

The tide has been turning for months. A Houthi offensive in September cost the government the Red Sea coast, including the port of Mocha, and left Taiz completely besieged. Government forces retook key ground near Bab al-Mandeb and say they killed or wounded 173 Houthi fighters in Operation Dawn of Yemen, but Mocha stayed out of reach. Now the Houthis are reported to be 60 kilometers (37 miles) north of Aden. Armed forces spokesman Majed al-Nuzaili called the retreat part of a wider tactical maneuver.

Civilians are paying the price. Houthi-affiliated media reported coalition air strikes on Sanaa and one death in an attack on a school in Taiz. Officials in Taiz are pleading for humanitarian corridors, and medical workers warn hospitals may stop operating within two days for lack of fuel and oxygen. Saudi Arabia said it shot down two Houthi drones aimed at the Mecca and Riyadh regions.

article.title: Explosion heard in north of Saudi capital
article.description: SAUDI-ARABIË - A powerful explosion was heard in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents reported,...
paragraphs: Abonneer Voorpagina Binnenland Buitenland English Sport Adverteer Contact SCCN Voorpagina Binnenland Buitenland English Sport Voorpagina Binnenland Buitenland English Sport Contact SCCN Adverteer Contact SCCN Abonneer Engels Explosion heard in north of Saudi capital SAUDI-ARABIË - A powerful explosion was heard in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents reported,...

following weeks of attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis. Residents told AFP there were no warnings sent to phones before the blast, which one person in the north of the capital described as "extremely loud". An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out. “Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening", one resident in northern Riyadh said. The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh's airport in the northeast of the city. In recent weeks the Houthis have launched strikes on a range of Saudi targets including airports, energy infrastructure, military sites and Riyadh's financial district.

In October, a deadly attack targeting King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed 14 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of flights for two weeks. Earlier on Wednesday, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had intercepted a cruise missile launched by the group towards the Riyadh area. The coalition, which backs neighbouring Yemen's internationally recognized government in its war with the Houthis, has battled a surge in attacks since hostilities reignited in July. The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world's poorest countries, had been dormant after a ceasefire was implemented in 2022, but the war sprang back to life in the summer. The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the government's interim capital, having made sweeping territorial gains in recent weeks. Since the summer, more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced by the fighting, according to the United Nations. ( Bssnews )

article.title: Houthi missile strikes Saudi Arabia’s 80‑storey PIF Tower, causing structural damage
article.description: A Houthi missile hit the PIF Tower in Riyadh’s financial district, shattering windows on several floors and bending the façade, but no injuries were reported.
paragraphs: Facebook X WhatsApp LinkedIn Copy link Advertisement Advertisement Saudi Arabia’s 80‑storey PIF Tower, the headquarters of the Public Investment Fund, was hit by a missile in a Houthi attack, according to Riyadh’s civil defence.
The impact caused material damage to several floors, blowing out windows across seven to eight levels and bending sections of the building’s metal façade.
State news agency SPA confirmed that no injuries were reported among occupants or passers‑by.
Three sources familiar with the incident said the tower was struck by a Houthi missile, while the Saudi‑led coalition said it had intercepted a missile threat over Riyadh and debris fell in the area.
The financial district surrounding the tower was closed to visitors after the strike, echoing a similar closure following a Houthi attack on an Aramco building less than two weeks earlier.
